  </div> <div>Date &amp; Location</div> Friday, April 24, 2026, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Zoom
  <div>Credits</div> <em>AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™</em> (7.00 hours), Non-Physician
  (7.00 hours) <div>Target Audience</div> <div> <em>Professions</em> - Naturopathic
  Physician, Nurse, Nurse Practitioner, Pharmacist, Physician, Physician Associate,
  Psychologist, Student</div> <div>Overview</div> <p>This course is designed specifically
  for primary care providers and focuses on delivering practical and current insights
  into frequently encountered cardiovascular conditions. Expert faculty from the University
  of Washington School of Medicine will lead participants through interactive, case-based
  lectures to foster engagement. The program will review the latest guidelines on
  hypertension, cholesterol management, heart disease prevention, atrial fibrillation,
  and heart failure. Key topics relevant to everyday practice, such as diagnosing
  and managing coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, valvular disorders,
  and supraventricular arrhythmias (including atrial fibrillation) will be addressed.
  The course will also cover practical considerations for using new anticoagulants
  and discuss the appropriate use of cardiovascular imaging during sessions on valvular
  disease, primary prevention, and chest pain evaluation with stress testing and coronary
  CT imaging. The day concludes with a comprehensive multiple-choice question review
  session led by the course chairs.</p> <div>Objectives</div> <ol> <li>Assess treatment
  strategies and manage high blood pressure based on updated clinical practice guidelines
  from 2025 (ACC/AHA)</li> <li>Apply cholesterol guidelines and the latest clinical
  trial data of novel cholesterol treatments to the management of patients with cardiac
  risk factors and atherosclerotic vascular disease</li> <li>Classify patients with
  chest pain and order the appropriate stress and imaging tests for your patients
  based on current guidelines</li> <li>Provide patients with evidence-based prescriptions
  for diet and exercise to lower risk of cardiovascular disease</li> <li>Evaluate
  and manage patients with valvular heart disease; identify which heart murmur patients
  should be referred for an echocardiogram and when patients should be referred for
  valve repair or replacement</li> <li>Support and treat patients with palpitations,
  and understand the appropriate use of heart rhythm monitors and when to refer patients
  to cardiology</li> <li>Interpret and treat atrial fibrillation and learn how to
  use direct oral anticoagulants to reduce stroke risk from atrial fibrillation, and
  when to refer to a specialist to consider rhythm control with antiarrhythmics or
  catheter ablation or left atrial appendage occlusion.</li> <li>Treat heart failure
  patients with the 4 pillars of guideline-directed medical therapy including novel
  treatments like angiotensin receptor-neprolysin inhibitors and SGLT2 inhibitors.</li>
  <li>Utilize novel diabetes drugs that have proven benefit in reducing cardiovascular
  events</li> </ol> <div>Registration</div> <p><strong><span>REGISTRATION IS NOW LIVE!</span></strong></p>

  <p>Continuing Medical Education at the University of Washington is a self-sustaining
  unit and does not depend on or receive public monies in support of its educational
  efforts. Fees for this course are estimated to cover the costs of conducting this
  course. These costs include salaries, registration and credit recording, instructional
  materials, transcript of credit, record keeping, faculty planning, evaluation, food
  and beverage during the conference, alcohol during the reception, and printed materials.
  If you have not received confirmation prior to the course start, please contact
  the CME office at <a><span>[email protected]</span></a>. Continuing Medical Education
  will not be responsible for expenses incurred by an individual who is not confirmed.</p>
  <p><strong><span>IMPORTANT PAYMENT INFORMATION</span></strong></p> <p>Per UW CME
  policy, you are not considered registered for the course until full payment has
  been received. Unpaid orders do not "reserve" spots for conferences. If you have
  an unpaid order when registration rates increase, your order will automatically
  increase to the higher late registration rate.</p> <p><strong><span>REFUND &amp;
  CANCELLATION POLICY</span></strong></p> <p>The Office of Continuing Medical Education
  must receive written notification of your cancellation by<strong> April</strong><span> 10,
  2026.</span> A $75 processing fee will be deducted from refund requests received
  by this date. No refunds will be issued following<strong> April 10, 2026</strong>.</p>

Join the 25th Annual Clinical Cardiology Pearls for Primary Care on April 24, 2026, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. via Zoom. This comprehensive webinar is tailored for primary care providers and will feature expert faculty from the University of Washington School of Medicine. Attendees can expect interactive, case-based lectures covering essential topics such as hypertension, cholesterol management, heart disease prevention, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure.

Participants will gain practical insights into diagnosing and managing common cardiovascular conditions, including coronary artery disease and valvular disorders. The program also includes a review session with multiple-choice questions to reinforce learning. Registration is now open, with fees starting at $125 for residents and students. Don’t miss this opportunity to enhance your knowledge and skills in cardiology.
